facts: The prior cache-reuse candidate trusted an extracted portable Python when python.exe merely existed.
The candidate caches only immutable bootstrap archives and rebuilds the extracted interpreter on every run.
Python 3.12.10 embeddable ZIP reuse and extraction are gated by its pinned upstream SHA-256.
The network-fetched get-pip.py execution path was removed. pip now bootstraps from the pinned pip 26.1.2 wheel published by PyPI, whose SHA-256 is verified before extraction.
Regression coverage asserts Python and pip artifact pinning, verification-before-extraction, absence of get-pip.py, no extracted-interpreter reuse, bounded retries, and fail-closed command handling.
Generic exact-head PR CI must rerun after this material change; affected self-hosted Local Runner runtime evidence is still a separate claim.
decision: Keep PR #380 Draft and deny merge until the new exact-head CI is green and the affected self-hosted Local Runner path is validated under its reviewed main-only execution contract. Supply-chain claims are limited to content verification of the pinned Python ZIP and pip wheel; no broader package-index or production authority is claimed.
lesson: A bootstrap repair must not replace availability risk with remote-code-execution trust: network-delivered bootstrap code must be content-bound before execution, and reusable caches must contain verifiable immutable inputs rather than mutable extracted runtimes.
security_boundary: No credentials, signing, billing, production deployment, live trading, financial action, or weakening of data/security gates is authorized.
